children: INDIAN AND PHILIPPINE OUTSOURCING SECTORS HANDLING AI HIT
If you had to look at countries where employment is most exposed to AI, India and the Philippines would be high on the list, with their large business outsourcing sectors.

But HSBC have taken a look at the numbers and it seems that so far at least business service exports from the two countries have held up well, no re-shoring, and even employment levels have not been heavily affected.

The data is better for exports, but HSBC find that since the final quarter of 2022, when ChatGPT 3.5 was released, India's other business services exports are up over 50%, with no obvious break in the upwards pointing curve.
The same is true in the Philippines, where export revenues from "other business services" where business process outsourcing sits, has risen steadily with no obvious collapse.

As to employment, in India, HSBC look at IT-related jobs and find there is no obvious impact from the arrival of AI: "since 2022, the number of jobs has steadily increased and is now well above where it stood before the pandemic."
Meanwhile, in the Philippines, HSBC say, "there has also been no 'apocalypse' in services jobs in the Philippines – if anything, employment has accelerated."
One important caveat they note is that the headline figures do not mean there are no adjustments beneath the surface
"Of course: some jobs have certainly been lost and many workers have encountered hardship as skill requirements in the job market have shifted"
"But," they say, overall, it is hard to argue that this is consistent with a “job apocalypse”.
So what's going on?
"It might be, of course, that AI has yet to make an impact," say HSBC

"But, it might also be that AI actually supports BPO to economies like India and the Philippines by making local workers more productive, quality control easier, and remote processing even more feasible."
(Alun John )
